audit.summary: vmicollect samples guest RAM on a fixed 5 s monotonic grid without jitter; a writer thread publishes delta snapshots with SHA-256 sidecars; scripts/collection.py runs one session and audits it with 24 RAM-side reasons plus 73 log-evidence checks. Corrupt or missing data is rejected. Weakness: timing and unproven gates. Event commands and guest crash loops can phase-lock with the grid; swap, lateness, collector warnings, unexecuted events and repaired rows are recorded but not gated; 19 of 24 RAM gates lack a negative test; no unprivileged end-to-end dry run exists.

facts.claim: Capture instants form a fixed grid: absolute CLOCK_MONOTONIC deadlines t_start + k*interval from collector start, no alignment, no jitter; an overrun drops whole slots (mode skip). The collector has an unused anti-aliasing option, schedule.jitter (deadline shifted by a random value in [-jitter, +jitter]*interval, no drift); the capture script passes only interval and cycle count.

The snapshot time stored in the sidecar is CLOCK_REALTIME at cycle start, while scheduling is monotonic. The audit's gap check (0 < dt <= max_gap_s), its period check (span within one interval of nominal over the whole session) and all event-window logic use this wall time.

One read of the 2 GiB guest: delta cycles p50 850 ms, p99 875 ms, max 895 ms; full snapshots 1.57-1.88 s, of which the eBPF copy itself is 312-336 ms (single VM, pilots 6 and 7). Campaign v6 maximum was 2009 ms at 318,946 pages. The VM is never paused (ops.pause is NULL), so pages of one snapshot span that duration.

facts.claim: Read failures are loud. A short read increments read_errors and filled_zero in the sidecar; a cycle that read zero bytes fails; a failed cycle, an unpublished snapshot or a lost log line gives exit code 4; the audit rejects any sidecar with read_errors, filled_zero or skipped_before, any cycle with total_ms >= interval and any wait for queue memory.

Stale or half-written files cannot be taken for data: snapshot and sidecar are written under dot-prefixed temporary names with O_EXCL and published with RENAME_NOREPLACE; the sidecar SHA-256 is computed from the bytes written and the audit re-hashes the file on disk. Session directory, raw directory and all JSON records are created exclusively.

A failed or aborted snapshot write breaks the delta chain and forces a full snapshot; the audit rejects a full snapshot outside the protocol cadence, and extraction raises on a memory-layout change. If the VM restarts, the collector re-attaches to the new PID with a warning only, but the runner compares QEMU PID/start time and guest boot identity after capture and aborts.

The RAM-side audit has 24 rejection reasons: no provenance, protocol hash, incomplete capture or guest identity, profile hash, collector hash or settings, mlock flag, bin width, no sidecars, image/sidecar count, snapshot count, sequence from zero, full cadence, image checksum, read errors/fill/missed slots, cycle >= period, queue wait, invalid inputs, integrity findings, coverage, positive control (pilot), sequence gap, timestamp gap, sampling period, log problems.

Only 5 of these 24 reasons have a test that makes them fire: invalid inputs, integrity findings and coverage (through analyze_windows), positive control, and log problems. audit_session itself is called by one test (one accepted case, one rejected for a traffic exit code). The strings of the other 19 reasons occur in tests only as report fixtures or comments.

recommendations: Randomize event phase: seeded offsets uniform in [0, interval_s) for every planned event start and duration instead of 30 s multiples, frozen in the plan; the audit reports the command phase of every event relative to the capture grid (scripts/collection.py:313-325).

Decide capture jitter explicitly before the pilot. Jitter (already implemented, vmicollect/src/sched.c:84-93) removes a persistent phase lock but not the expected number of torn reads, and it makes sample spacing unequal. If used, store the realized interval per row and gate lateness against the jittered deadline. If not used, the periodicity detector and the forbidden-period check are mandatory.

Move the swap ban into the code path: preflight verifies memory.swap.max = 0 on the QEMU cgroup and zero swapped guest RAM, records both and refuses otherwise; campaign init pins the setting the same way it pins vm.swappiness (scripts/campaign.py:358-359).

Add the missing audit gates with thresholds pre-registered from the pilot: lateness, cycle-time margin, swap-in and major faults, monitor process presence, WARN allow-list, executed events with effect predicates, a cap on rule-closed rows, periodicity of flagged rows, mandatory sidecar keys.

Build the gate self-test (mutation matrix) for all 24 RAM-side reasons and all 73 log keys, keep it both as a pytest module and as a stored result record, and require a matching passing record at campaign init. The probes run in this review can serve as its first draft.

Create an unprivileged end-to-end dry run: the runner with a file-backend collector on a synthetic or replayed image and a stub labctl, executing preflight, warmup, capture, events, evidence, audit, archive and corpus build; then repeat with injected faults (killed collector, dropped snapshot, stalled disk, clock step, failed event, swap flag) and check each expected verdict. It changes measurement code, so it must land before the pilot.

Redesign the pilot as a rehearsal: both VMs concurrently, all seven event types and the positive control per VM, a no-event stretch as negative control, concurrent audit and archive, worst-case full snapshot. Write pass criteria first and store one pilot report per criterion; keep pilot directories outside campaign and corpus.

Measure and record guest periodicities in the pilot: restart period of each crash-looping unit, worker round under the lock, PostgreSQL checkpoint and autovacuum intervals, kernel writeback and ext4 commit intervals. Compare each with 5 s and decide whether to change RestartSec or the event design before the campaign.

Unify the acceptance rule (loader, audit, pilot gate; both session lengths) and freeze thresholds, replacement limit and continuation rule before the pilot, with each number justified from mechanism rather than from past rejection counts.

Add a campaign-level early-warning stop rule: after every session compare flagged-row rate, cycle time and lateness per event type with the pilot values and stop on a pre-registered excess, instead of discovering a systematic cause at the replacement limit.

Have the collector record its effective schedule settings and a build identifier in each sidecar, and audit against those values instead of capture.json, which only echoes the runner's own environment.

Put the per-session timing evidence (event command phase, lateness, cycle time, flagged rows by event type, swap counters) into the campaign report as one table, so that a future resonance or host interference is visible without a separate forensic record.
open_questions: Does the model design tolerate jittered sampling (unequal steps), or must the 5 s grid stay exact? This decides between capture jitter and source-side fixes plus a periodicity detector.
Were past pilots run with both VMs capturing concurrently and with a background audit or archive? This cannot be derived from the repository.

What is the real restart period of hyptcn-lab@catalog under zla_konfiguracia_sluzby, and are the guest's kernel writeback and ext4 commit intervals at their usual 5 s defaults? No record and no install step states them (unverified).
Should rows closed by the prev/tail/meet rules count toward invalid_rows.max, or be excluded from training and calibration?
Is a coverage gate of 0.77 acceptable when the lost windows concentrate in event periods, the part of normal behaviour the events are meant to teach?
How many pilot sessions per VM are affordable? Seven event types plus a control need at least three 600-cycle sessions per VM under the current spacing rules.

facts.claim: Eight memory columns come only from the collector sidecar: mem_changed_ratio (changed/backed pages), mem_bins_active (share of bins with a change), mem_changed_max, mem_changed_p95 (nearest rank over bins), mem_changed_spread (normalised entropy of changes over bins), mem_entropy_mean (weighted by changed pages), mem_entropy_max, mem_zero_ratio (zero/backed pages). The first four measure amount of change per interval, the next three its distribution and content; mem_zero_ratio is a level. None was constant in v6 (relative std 3.6-52 %).

Twelve object columns: proc_total = closed init_task.tasks walk (thread-group leaders); proc_user/proc_kernel split by mm == 0; proc_new/proc_gone = pid-set differences against the previous valid snapshot; mod_total/mod_delta from the modules list; sock_total/sock_listen/sock_estab count socket descriptors per process, so a shared socket counts once per holder; proc_wx/proc_memfd count processes with W+X pages or memfd files.

Per-bin inputs are read from the same sidecar; changed_ratio is recomputed from integer page counts; has_changed is an input mask, never a target. One TCN is shared across bins. Score = 0.5 * mean squared error over the global columns + 0.5 * maximum over bins of the masked error; every global column is both input and target.

A row is invalid when any of the four traversals (processes, modules, sockets, memory patterns) reports truncated, or the sidecar counts RAM read errors or zero-filled pages. Structural faults (missing sidecar, layout or bin-identity change, sidecar/header mismatch) abort extraction with an error instead of producing a row.

open_questions: Should columns that are constant in benign data (mod_total, mod_delta, proc_wx, proc_memfd) stay model inputs or become a separate rule channel? The answer decides what the thesis may claim the network detects.
Can QEMU be cold-started for every group, or may mem_zero_ratio and per-bin zero_ratio be dropped or differenced? Without one of these, role and QEMU age stay aligned by construction.
Is capture jitter acceptable? It breaks aliasing but makes the delta interval variable, so the contract would need the interval as an input and max_gap_s would have to be re-derived.
Are tolerated invalid rows meant to reach training archives (the trainer then skips them), or must accepted sessions be fully valid? The code currently says both.

With events in every role, which event types are expected to stay alarm-free and which may alarm? The v6 model alarmed on 60 of 111 benign events; the expected response per type should be pre-registered.
May redundant columns be removed and proc_kernel redefined before the freeze, given that schema /4 was fixed on 2026-11-14 and no corpus depends on it any more?

How do swapped-out or unreadable guest pages appear in the memory columns (read error, zero fill, or stale content)? Unverified in this layer; root cause 1 suggests it matters for mem_* and for row validity.

audit.summary: This layer trains a 12,967-parameter two-branch causal TCN next-frame predictor on benign sessions, scores windows by squared z-error (mean over global features plus worst bin), thresholds at a pooled calibration quantile and votes 3-of-5. Role isolation during fitting is sound. Main weakness: nothing shows the network beats trivial predictors or per-feature thresholds; stored evidence is benign FAR only, quasi-constant counts and one bin dominate the score, no baseline results exist, the test-once guard is bypassable, and training rejects v5-shaped corpora. Paths are relative to /home/eh/Desktop/hyptcn3.

facts.claim: Predictor = global branch TCNPrediktor (20 behavioural features in, 20 out) plus one TCN (4 per-bin channels in, 3 out) shared across all memory bins; 16 channels, kernel 3, 4 residual blocks (dilations 1,2,4,8), dropout 0.1, two causal left-padded convolutions per block. Bins are folded into the batch axis, so the bin branch has no bin identity and sees neither other bins nor global features; the global branch sees no per-bin data.

Instantiated locally: predictor has 12,967 trainable parameters (global 7,140, bin 5,827); the workload classifier 7,414 with 6 classes. Receptive field is 61 rows against 31 context rows (window 32; the last row is the target and is excluded from the input). The v6 bundle had 18 global features (12,805 predictor parameters).

facts.claim: Loss = 0.5*mean(global squared error) + 0.5*mean over bins of masked MSE (entropy counted only where has_changed=1), next-frame target. Adam lr 0.001, batch 32, default 10 epochs. Predictor and classifier losses are summed and their gradients clipped jointly at norm 5, so predictor updates and random-number consumption depend on the classifier.

Anomaly score = 0.5*mean over global features of squared z-error + 0.5*MAX over bins of masked MSE; the loss uses the mean over bins, the score the maximum. Bundle.score returns score, a scalar global_error, bin_errors per bin and the activity class; per-global-feature errors are neither returned nor stored in events.jsonl.

Threshold = empirical quantile (1-fpr, method 'higher', default fpr 0.01) of all calibration-role window scores pooled; at least max(100, 10/fpr) scores are required, counted in windows, not sessions. Alarm = at least k=3 of the last n=5 scores above threshold, evaluated only once 5 scores exist; an alarm event is the rising edge; history resets at every barrier (gap, chain change, invalid row, full snapshot). There is no other hysteresis or cooldown.

Checkpoint = epoch with the lowest dev-role loss, chosen separately for predictor and classifier. One seed sets random, numpy and torch. The final model is seed 0; tcn/seedy.py trains seeds 1-4 with the identical procedure and summarises mean, sd, min and max, and its summary refuses test_benign results. No deterministic-algorithms flag is set.

The normalizer is fitted once on train-role rows that are valid, have a predecessor and are not full snapshots: per-feature mean and std for global features; per-bin channels pooled over all bins (entropy over changed bins only). A std at or below machine epsilon is replaced by 1.0, so a train-constant feature keeps its raw units.

During fitting, test_benign feature archives are never opened: the loop skips the role, a unit test patches the loader to assert it, and index validation enforces disjoint boots and groups plus chronological role order. The manifest field test_feature_arrays_loaded is a hard-coded False literal, not a measurement.

v6 training (seed 0, 10 epochs): dev prediction loss fell monotonically from 0.3297 to 0.2745 and the selected predictor epoch is 10 of 10, so training stopped on budget, not convergence. Classifier dev loss rose from epoch 1 (1.82 to 3.06) while its train loss fell to 0.012; selected epoch 1. Threshold 14.430 from 7,872 calibration scores, exceedance fraction 0.0099, 1 calibration alarm event (0.091/h).

Stored TCN results on the corpus are benign only. Final test_benign: 1 model alarm event in 10.93 scored hours, 0.091/h (95% interval 0.0023-0.51), 12 sessions, 2 groups. Dev: 1 event in 5.47 h, 0.183/h. Workload classifier window accuracy 0.663 on dev and 0.446 on test_benign (5 of 12 sessions correct by majority).

Events-v3 replay with the v6 bundle (events absent from its training): clean operation 1 alarm event in 21.26 h (0.047/h); during events 62 alarm events (5.63/h). By type: zamok_tabulky 15/15, zla_konfiguracia_sluzby 15/15, zataz_pamate 15/16, restart_databazy 14/16, zla_konfiguracia_nginx 1/17, restart_sluzby 0/16, udrzba_zaloha 0/16. risks.title: Score can reduce to per-feature thresholds
risks.description: The score is a sum of squared z-residuals weighted by 1/std^2 plus the worst single bin. Quasi-constant counts get tiny stds, so one unit of surprise in one count decides the comparison with the threshold; proc_new, proc_gone, mod_delta and mem_changed_* are already first differences. If the network predicts roughly the last value or the mean, the detector is 'a count changed in 3 of 5 snapshots'. Whether learning adds anything is unmeasured.

risks.title: Test-once guard is bypassable; positive sets are unguarded
risks.description: Replay of a test_benign archive with any bundle or baseline is unrestricted and prints alarm counts. The ledger is keyed by file path, checks only that tcn/eval.py is committed, and accepts any bundle trained on the corpus, so seeds or hyperparameters could be chosen after looking. Keep test archives sealed (root-owned) until then; refuse replay of archives whose sha belongs to a sealed role; apply the same once-only rule to event and malware sets; require a clean tree.

risks.title: Existing baselines are strawmen or differently fed

Stored results fit this (single service restart 0 of 16, backup 0 of 16, nginx misconfiguration 1 of 17; sustained faults 14-15 of 15-16), but per-window exceedances are not stored, so the cause is unverified. The evaluator labels k times the period (15 s) as the minimum possible delay; the record shows 2.6 s.

audit.summary: The evaluation layer turns safeguard replays into alarm-event counts: false alarms per hour with exact Poisson intervals, per-event-type tests against clean operation, a classifier test, anomaly baselines, a malware-style detection evaluator and an A/B/A overhead tool. Every interval treats events as independent and the boot group is never resampled. Main weakness for v5: with events inside normal, false alarms fall by construction; nothing measures remaining sensitivity, no primary metric or sample-size target exists, and the single-use test guard can be bypassed. Paths below are relative to /home/eh/Desktop/hyptcn3.

facts.claim: `tcn.eval far` counts alarm events (rising edges of the k-of-n rule), not windows above threshold. It reports events per observed hour and per scored hour with a two-sided exact Garwood (Poisson) interval, the unscored time share and a Pearson dispersion test across sessions. Its recorded assumptions: events independent, between-boot variability not in the interval, per-scenario and per-group intervals not simultaneous.
facts.evidence: tcn/eval.py:216-221 (interval), 224-265 (events, unscored share), 268-294 (rate, dispersion), 198-206 (assumptions); same text in data/results/safeguard_far_test_benign_v6_20261104.json key values.predpoklady.

facts.claim: The methodology names the boot group or run as the independent unit, never the overlapping window. The code never resamples by session or group: all intervals and p-values are exact Poisson, binomial or chi-square formulas on pooled counts; the group count is only printed. The single bootstrap in the repository (E5) resamples 30 s clusters inside blocks. Header n means sessions in FAR records, windows in the classifier record, blocks in E5.

E2 (step A) and E2' (step B) use `tcn.eval udalosti`: a window belongs to an event when its 32 rows overlap the event interval, a 300 s afterglow follows, the rest is clean operation. Output: false alarms per hour per type and class, a one-sided conditional exact binomial test against clean operation, alarm delay and decay. E2 rule: no more false alarms than in clean operation means usable, otherwise step B. E2' (role test_benign, --final) has no numeric success criterion.

VO6 is `tcn.klasifikator`: a new classifier over the frozen bundle, trained on dataset 1 (train, dev) plus the odd boot groups of dataset 2 and tested on the even groups. Metrics: window accuracy and macro-F1 without interval, majority vote per event occurrence and per session with Clopper-Pearson intervals. Checkpoint selection uses dev profiles only. No decision rule and no single-use guard exist for it.

facts.claim: The alarm threshold is the (1 - fpr) quantile of all pooled calibration window scores (fpr default 0.01), followed by a 3-of-5 rule. The only sample requirement is max(100, 10/fpr) = 1000 window scores; there is no minimum number of sessions or boots. fpr, k, n, epochs and seed are command-line defaults of `safeguard train`; the v5 protocol draft holds no evaluation parameters.

facts.claim: Corpus validation requires roles to be separated in time (train before dev before calibration before test_benign). The previous iteration recorded a feature drifting along that order: session medians of mem_zero_ratio were 0.478 to 0.700 in train, 0.4615 to 0.4648 in dev, 0.4269 to 0.4375 in calibration and 0.236 to 0.320 in the later event groups 5 to 8; 42 of 45 E2 sessions lay below the training range.

Prior, steady operation, bundle v6. test_benign: 1 model alarm event in 39360 scored s (10.93 h) = 0.0915/h, Garwood 0.0023 to 0.510; 12 sessions, 2 boots (0 and 1 events); dispersion X2 11.0, df 11, p 0.443. dev: 1 event in 19680 s = 0.183/h (0.0046 to 1.019), 6 sessions, 1 boot. Calibration: 1 event in 10.93 scorable hours, threshold 14.43.

Prior, clean operation between events (bundle v6 on campaign events-v3): 1 event in 76535 scored s (21.26 h) = 0.047/h, Garwood 0.0012 to 0.262; afterglow 0 events in 31430 s, upper bound 0.423/h; 45 sessions, 8 boots. Clean operation was 52 % of scored time, events 27 %, afterglow 21 % (my ratio of the recorded seconds). Pooled with test_benign and dev: 3 events in 37.7 h, about 0.08/h (my sum).

Prior, during events, model trained on steady data only: 62 alarm events in 39635 scored s = 5.63/h (4.32 to 7.22). 60 of 111 executed occurrences had a model alarm: restart_databazy 14/16, zamok_tabulky 15/15, zataz_pamate 15/16, zla_konfiguracia_sluzby 15/15, zla_konfiguracia_nginx 1/17, restart_sluzby 0/16, udrzba_zaloha 0/16. Median delay 12.7 to 12.9 s; no alarm lasted to the end of the afterglow.

The event response was near-deterministic per type, not Poisson: the dispersion test over 107 session-type units gave X2 64.8 on 106 df (p 0.99945, under-dispersed). Between boots the share of occurrences with an alarm ranged only from 0.50 to 0.57 over 8 groups (my aggregation of the per-occurrence list). For clean operation no between-boot spread can be estimated: one event per data set.

In the accepted sessions of the previous iteration unscored time was structural and constant: 64 of 720 rows per session (0.0889), the window warm-up after each full snapshot. By category it varied: clean operation 0.096, restart_databazy 0.155, udrzba_zaloha 0.146, zataz_pamate 0.139. Input errors and sensor gaps were zero by acceptance, not by measurement.

The v5 draft admits sessions with up to 3 invalid process-walk rows and score coverage down to 0.77 (v4: 0.85). One isolated invalid row removes 33 windows (165 s of scoring). In campaign v4c, 9 of 13 invalid rows fell inside the table-lock event: unscored time is concentrated at events, not spread at random.

The per-occurrence record of `tcn.eval udalosti` holds no count of scored rows. An occurrence whose rows are all unscored is reported as executed with alarm_modelu false, indistinguishable from a scored occurrence without alarm (confirmed by calling priebeh_udalosti on 40 unscored rows in a scratch script). The per-type rate uses scored seconds as its denominator.

Single-use guard: role test_benign runs only with --final, and --final only with test_benign. --final needs git and requires that tcn/eval.py itself is not listed by git status. After the output file is opened, a marker `<corpus path>.test_benign-final.json` (for events `...-final-udalosti.json`) is created in exclusive mode; an existing marker aborts and removes the output. The marker stores date, output path, commit, evaluator hash and bundle manifest hash.

facts.claim: `safeguard replay --archive` accepts any archive with any bundle, has no role check and writes status.json with alarm_events. The v6 final evaluation replayed all 12 test_benign sessions first and called --final afterwards, so test alarm counts existed on disk before the guard was consumed; nothing limits repeated replays with other bundles.

The held-out groups of dataset 2 have no code guard. `tcn.eval udalosti` on an events index needs no --final and writes no marker; `tcn.klasifikator eval` and `tcn.eval malver` only refuse to overwrite their --out file. The plan's statement that even test_events groups are evaluated once is procedural only. Multi-seed summaries reject test_benign results by design.

The pilot control kontrola_wx_memfd is gated on extractor output: every row inside the control must list both patterns. Nothing checks the model score. Features constant in training get scale 1, and the score is 0.5 x mean of 20 global squared errors + 0.5 x maximum bin error, so proc_wx = proc_memfd = 1 adds about 0.05 against the v6 threshold of 14.43 (my arithmetic, assuming both stay zero in training as recorded so far).

risks.title: False alarm rate can fall by construction while sensitivity is unmeasured
risks.description: In v5 events are part of normal in every role, and the threshold is a pooled window quantile of the calibration role. Event windows were about 27 % of scored time before, so the 0.99 quantile will sit inside the event score distribution. E2' will then show few false alarms at events whatever the network learned, and the A versus B comparison will look like success. Nothing in the plan measures what the raised threshold still detects.

risks.title: Single-use guard does not hold and results leak before it is consumed
risks.description: The guard is a marker file keyed on the corpus path in a git-ignored directory. A copy of the index, a deleted marker or a direct function call repeats the final test; replays of test sessions are unguarded and show alarm counts first. Dataset 2 test groups and the classifier test have no guard at all. Deleting data sets also deletes the markers.

risks.protocol_control: A ledger committed to git, keyed on the sorted features_sha256 of the test sessions, covering both data sets. One command replays and evaluates in a single step for a model list whose manifest hashes were committed beforehand. Require a clean tree for all measurement and model code plus a freeze tag. Test-role archives stay unreplayed until that command; every opening is logged.

The realistic outcomes are baselines reported only on dev, which selected every network checkpoint, or a bypassed guard. No code builds the comparison table or a paired difference.

State before collection which model carries the claim and which are comparisons.

risks.title: 'More than thresholds on single variables' is not testable with the present baselines
risks.description: The comparison set has no last-value predictor, no per-feature threshold rule, no rate-matched random alarm and no attribution of which score term fired. The score is a mean over 20 global errors plus the maximum single-bin error, so an alarm may be one bin or one counter crossing a level. The z-score baseline averages over columns and would hide exactly that. The earlier project was retracted after a simple baseline matched the model.
risks.evidence: tcn/porovnanie.py:87, 100-106; safeguard/model.py:16, 84, 91-92; HONESTY.md:133.
risks.protocol_control: Add to the same replay path: last-value predictor with the identical score and k-of-n rule; per-feature quantile thresholds; best single feature; random alarms at matched rate; TCN with time order shuffled inside the window. Log per alarm which term and feature exceeded. Pre-registered criterion: the TCN must beat the best dumb rule on surrogate alarm share at equal clean false alarm rate, shown per boot.

risks.title: Boot group is the declared unit but no interval uses it
risks.description: Garwood and Clopper-Pearson intervals and the rate tests treat alarm events, occurrences or sessions as independent; the threshold is a quantile over overlapping windows from 4 boots; E5 intervals resample 30 s clusters. With 4 test boots a boot-level interval is barely possible, so narrow intervals and p-values near 1e-17 overstate the evidence. An earlier p-value from non-independent windows was retracted.

risks.title: Planned test size cannot support the likely claims
risks.description: Four test boots of six one-hour sessions give about 11 clean scored hours (my estimate from the previous time shares). At the prior rates 0.05 to 0.09/h an upper bound below 0.5/h is reached with probability 0.60 to 0.37; below 0.2/h it cannot be reached. Each event type gets about 8 to 9 occurrences: zero alarms in 8 only bounds the alarm probability below 0.37. No document derives the allocation from a target.

risks.description: v5 accepts sessions with coverage down to 0.77, and invalid rows cluster at event boundaries, where alarms previously started about 13 s after onset. One invalid row blanks 165 s. Event false alarms and any surrogate detection would be biased toward 'quiet'.

risks.title: Chronological roles alias role with drift
risks.description: Roles are collected strictly in sequence and the guest state drifts over days. Before, the calibration role lay entirely outside the training range of one memory feature, and later sessions further still. A threshold calibrated in one regime and tested in another measures drift as much as the model; with events in training the same shift can hide or create alarms.

risks.title: Event false alarms are measured with a rate that does not fit them
risks.description: At events the model gave about one alarm per occurrence regardless of duration; counts were strongly under-dispersed. A per-hour rate then depends on the chosen event length and on the 155 s window tail added to exposure, and Poisson intervals and rate-ratio tests do not describe the data.

risks.title: An under-trained or trivial predictor would not be noticed
risks.description: The only real training stopped at the epoch limit with dev loss still falling, and nothing records how the prediction error compares with trivial predictors. A TCN that merely copies the last value, or one that has not converged, yields the same kind of bundle and the same kind of false alarm record. Baseline networks share the 10-epoch default, so a comparison may reflect budget, not architecture.

recommendations: Write config/evaluation-v5.json before the dry run and hash it into the protocol and every bundle manifest: questions, one primary metric each, alpha, fpr, k, n, stopping rule, seeds, afterglow, model list, the definition of an evaluable occurrence, exclusion rules and decision rules. The evaluator reads its parameters only from this file and refuses a bundle trained with other values.

Proposed primary metrics: (P1) model alarm events per observed hour outside events, with a per-boot table; (P2) share of evaluable event occurrences with a model alarm, per type, Holm over seven; (P3) share of held-out benign surrogate occurrences alarmed within a fixed horizon at the frozen threshold, against the chance probability from control spans. Availability (unscored share per category) is a gate reported with each.

Benign surrogate anomalies without malware: keep at least two event types and a few new benign behaviours (graded memory load, many W+X processes, burst of listening sockets, bulk file rewrite) out of dataset 1 entirely and run them only in held-out boots. Evaluate with the existing `tcn.eval malver` machinery (scenario and control runs, new config). Call the result 'sensitivity to unseen benign behaviour'; durations must span several capture periods (docs/LIMITACIE.md:1069-1119).

Cheapest surrogate: leave one event type out. The previous model, never trained on events, alarmed on 59 of 62 occurrences of four types and 1 of 49 of the other three (summary record values.by_type). Training v5 variants without one type each, on train, dev and calibration only, gives a detection-like number per type with no extra collection. Pre-register the types, the horizon and the expected direction.

Add the dumb rules and ablations to tcn/porovnanie.py so they pass through the same Detector and evaluator, and add one comparison command that prints TCN, seeds and all baselines in a single table with paired per-boot differences. A baseline that matches the TCN is the result and goes into the conclusion (HONESTY.md:76-80).

Use more boots for the same hours: for example 8 test boots of 3 sessions instead of 4 of 6, and at least 6 calibration boots. Decide in advance whether afterglow time counts as normal operation in P1; in the previous data that raises the usable exposure from 52 % to 73 % of scored time (events record, values.merane.*.spolu.skorovany_s).

Seal the held-out data: replay and evaluation as one command, a git-tracked ledger keyed on test session content hashes, model list committed before opening, clean tree required for safeguard/, tcn/, features/ and guestparse/ (today only tcn/eval.py:1221 is checked). Extend the same guard to the even test_events groups, `tcn.klasifikator eval` and the surrogate evaluation.

Report blind time honestly: per-occurrence scored coverage, rates per observed hour as headline, unscored share by category, and a worst-case variant in which non-evaluable occurrences count as alarms. For kernel integrity print the share of rows where the check was conclusive before any alarm count; in the last test record it was 0 of 8640 rows (values.dane_prijatim_korpusu).

Calibration robustness: require a minimum number of calibration boots, record the share of calibration windows that are event windows, and print the leave-one-boot-out threshold range in the bundle manifest. Decide before collection whether the threshold comes from all windows or from clean windows only, because that choice fixes what E2' can show.

Stage gates for the evaluation layer. Dry run: full chain on synthetic and rehearsal data with known answers. Pilot (never in the data set): replay it with a rehearsal bundle, write down beforehand whether the detector is expected to alarm on the positive control, check per-occurrence scored coverage of the pilot events, reproduce the evaluator output from the archive. Campaign: no evaluator change without a new tag and a logged reason.

E5: treat the repetition as the unit. Plan at least 6 to 8 repetitions across at least two boots or call the result descriptive; update the defaults to the v5 protocol and bundle, run it after training, and fix the acceptable overhead before the run (HONESTY.md:70-74).

audit.summary: Paths are relative to /home/eh/Desktop/hyptcn3. The layer is a five-route shop API (nginx, three threaded Python services, a 1 s queue worker, PostgreSQL) driven by a seeded closed-loop generator in six stationary scenarios (1.5-50 req/s), with 2-3 benign events per session injected through the guest agent. Main weakness: the baseline is static and error-free, so events are separable by single-variable thresholds; schedules sit on a 30 s grid commensurate with the 5 s capture; events are accepted without proof of effect; the pilot exercises 2 of 7 event types.

facts.claim: Stack: nginx :8080 proxies to three ThreadingHTTPServer processes (catalog 8081, auth 8082, orders 8083) plus a queue worker; PostgreSQL over a UNIX socket with fixed pools (12 connections per HTTP service, 1 for the worker, none for auth). Each VM has 2048 MiB and 2 vCPUs.

The API has five routes. Data: five products, one orders table, one heartbeat row. Request bodies are capped at 8 KiB, identities are passwordless. There are no static files, uploads, search, cache, sessions, mail or outbound calls.

Generator is a closed loop: N threads, each sends 1-2 requests (1-4 in a burst iteration), then sleeps uniform 0.5-1.5 s (0.15-0.6 s after a burst). Per-worker RNG is Random(seed + 1009*index); one user per worker (demo0..demo7); a new HTTP connection per request. Decisions are seeded, timing is not reproducible.

Request mix: catalog_share -> GET /api/catalog; 0.95 - catalog - write -> GET /api/orders; write_share -> POST /api/orders; a fixed 5 % -> /healthz; product uniform 1-5, quantity 1-3. The six scenarios differ only in workers (1-8), burst probability (0-1) and the two shares; quiet, steady and bursty share one mix.

Measured rates in benign-v6 (scenario parameters identical in the v1-v5 configs, 8 sessions each): quiet 1.5, steady 7.7, write_heavy 16.6, read_heavy 17.6, mixed 18.7, bursty 49.9 req/s. Request totals of one scenario differ by at most 3.1 % between sessions; 3,225,975 requests, 0 errors.

facts.claim: Guest background work is only the worker loop: every 1 s plus round time it completes up to 50 pending orders, upserts a heartbeat and deletes completed orders older than one day (no index supports that predicate). Distribution timers (apt, logrotate, man-db, fstrim, e2scrub, dpkg-db-backup, tmpfiles-clean) are disabled or masked.

Guest fixed periods and ratio to 5 s: RestartSec 3 s (0.6), statement_timeout 3 s (0.6), internal fetch timeout 4 s (0.8), handler socket timeout 10 s (2), worker pause 1 s (0.2), heartbeat staleness 15 s (3), pool connect_timeout 5 s (1), TimeoutStopSec 10 s (2), token lifetime 3600 s (720).

nginx: access-log flush 2 s (0.4; five flushes = two intervals), proxy_connect_timeout 2 s (0.4), proxy_read_timeout 10 s (2). No upstream keepalive is configured, so each proxied request opens a new loopback connection (nginx default behaviour, not checked in the guest).

Composite periods: the old worker crash loop was 3 s timeout + 3 s RestartSec + 0.25 s start = 6.25 s, so four periods equal five intervals (measured 6.242-6.251 s in 20 sessions). After the staged fix the worker stays alive and retries about every 4 s (five periods = four intervals) with no process churn. lab/tests/test_worker.py: 3 passed locally.

Host fixed periods: client timeout 10 s (2), signal poll 0.2 s, summary interval 5 s (exactly 1), log flush 1 s and fsync every 5 s (1), token refresh 3000 s (600), runner loop 1 s, foreign-generator scan 15 s (3), host monitor 1 s, warm-up 120 s (24), guest-exec poll 0.3 s, agent timeout 60 s.

Event schedule: 2-3 events per session, first at 600 s or later, gap at least 600 s, tail 600 s, durations 120-360 s in 30 s steps, block shift in 30 s steps. In the v5 plan all 238 event starts are multiples of 30 s (six intervals); none of the 96 sessions is event-free; events cover 16.3 % of measured time.

facts.claim: Event zla_konfiguracia_sluzby: a drop-in with a misspelled service argument, daemon-reload, restart of catalog. The process exits at once and systemd restarts it every RestartSec for the whole 120-360 s (roughly 37-115 start/exit cycles, derived; exact period unverified). Stop removes the drop-in, resets the failure state and restarts catalog.

Event zla_konfiguracia_nginx rewrites the catalog upstream port 8081 to 8091, runs nginx -t and a reload (worker processes are replaced; count unverified); catalog requests fail until stop restores the file. Event restart_sluzby is one `systemctl restart hyptcn-lab@orders` at start and nothing at stop.

Event restart_databazy is one `systemctl restart postgresql` at start; Requires= makes systemd restart all four lab units, and the log audit expects restarts of postgresql@15-main and the four apps. It is the largest process burst: all PostgreSQL processes including 25 pooled backends and four Python services (counts derived).

Event zamok_tabulky: a detached psql holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on orders (pg_sleep 3600). Orders statements fail after 3 s, the heartbeat goes stale after 15 s and /healthz returns 503. Extra persistent processes: runuser, psql, one backend. Stop kills the process group and terminates the backend.

Event udrzba_zaloha is a detached pipeline (pg_dump | gzip, then tar -czf of /etc, sync): a short burst of short-lived processes, after which the window is idle; stop deletes the output. Event zataz_pamate is a python3 process (user nobody) holding 400 MiB of touched memory, about 20 % of guest RAM, until stop.

Every event start and stop travels through qemu-guest-agent as `bash -lc` running python3 udalosti.py, which ends with six `systemctl show` calls and a health probe; stop also polls health up to 30 times at 1 s. This footprint is identical for all event types.

Event acceptance: executed = start ok and stop ok and health 200. Detached events return right after Popen with output discarded. Inside a window (start - 1 s to stop + 60 s) the audit tolerates any failed request, traceback and nginx error line, and never checks that the expected effect occurred. Only the pilot control verifies its own effect.

E2 on events-v3 (model trained without events) alarmed in restart_databazy 14/16, zamok_tabulky 15/15, zataz_pamate 15/16, zla_konfiguracia_sluzby 15/15, but restart_sluzby 0/16, udrzba_zaloha 0/16, zla_konfiguracia_nginx 1/17. zamok_tabulky then included the worker crash loop that the staged fix removes, so its old footprint no longer applies.

Pilot: role pilot runs only the protocol's pilot events (zla_konfiguracia_nginx, restart_databazy) plus the W+X/memfd control, 600 cycles, scenario default steady. Five of seven event types, including the table lock and the crash-loop event, are never exercised before a campaign.

The v5 draft plan equals the v4 plan: the same 96 seeds, event schedules, scenario order and VM assignment; only the group prefix differs. Seeds derive from sha256(role/repetition) alone; the event RNG and traffic worker 0 both use Random(session seed); a replacement repeats the same seed.

recommendations: Make the profile a first-class protocol field: scenario = profile + seeded parameters; keep today's API as profile `api`. Generator profiles as small classes in scripts/host_traffic.py; scenario validation in scripts/collection.py. All four additions below fit the existing stack (stdlib, nginx, PostgreSQL, systemd) in roughly 700-900 new lines including tests.

E-shop profile: catalogue of a few thousand seeded products with paging and search (ILIKE), cart, checkout writing orders and items, static files served by nginx. Generator: user sessions as a funnel with think time and Zipf product choice. About 130 lines services, 25 schema, 10 nginx/install, 160 generator, 100 tests. Moves mem_changed_*, per-bin change and entropy, sock_estab and sock_total; proc_* stay flat.

Corporate profile: password login (hashlib.scrypt) with login bursts, document upload and download on disk, periodic report job from a systemd timer with RandomizedDelaySec, scripted admin maintenance. About 120 lines services, 15 schema, 100 lab/jobs.py, 20 unit files, 130 generator, 50 admin script. Moves proc_new, proc_gone, proc_total, proc_user, entropy features (uploads), mem_zero_ratio, sock_estab.

Batch/ETL profile: low HTTP rate plus queued jobs run by the worker as subprocesses: bulk load, aggregation, VACUUM ANALYZE, export piped to gzip, a small multiprocessing pool. About 120 lines lab/jobs.py, 25 worker, 12 schema, 30 generator. Moves mem_changed_ratio, mem_changed_max, mem_bins_active, entropy, mem_zero_ratio, proc_new and proc_gone. It supplies the multi-step benign pattern a sequence model can learn.

Mostly idle profile: one monitoring probe every 30-90 s with jitter and rare user requests; about 30 generator lines, no service change. It fixes the floor of mem_changed_* and shows whether silence itself raises alarms. Keep at least one request in the measured phase or relax the `no_measure_requests` check deliberately.

Replace fixed-parameter closed loops by open-loop session arrivals (Poisson) under a seeded piecewise rate envelope: ramps, a compressed day and night cycle, a short flash crowd. Add heavy-tailed think time, 1-3 % client errors (404, 401, 400) and a mix of keep-alive and one-shot connections. Write the envelope into the log header. About 120 lines.

Randomise with recorded seeds: event start (continuous, uniform over the capture phase), duration, count including event-free sessions, type order; arrival times, rate envelope, think time, session length, user and product choice, payload size; token refresh; worker pause; restart delay; timer jobs. Keep fixed and recorded: capture interval and profile parameters.

Add a resonance check to code readiness: a registry of every period with its source line, and a test that fails when period divided by capture interval is within tolerance of p/q for small q unless the period is jittered. In the guest: move autovacuum_naptime off multiples of 5 s, jitter the worker pause, bound restart loops.

Give every event an effect predicate and a measured active phase. Add the no-op harness control and a sham event (window labelled, nothing run) that the audit must reject, so the tolerance inside event windows is itself tested. Reject sessions whose events lack their effect.

Run a workload-only dry run before any capture: every profile and event type against both VMs, checking achieved rate band, route mix, error share, restart periods, event phases and return to the defined guest state. Then the pilot matrix (all events, lightest and heaviest profile, swept phases), excluded from the dataset by role and directory.

Use the traffic interval log as a dummy model: predict each feature from requests per 5 s and route counts of the same interval. Features explained by this regression carry load, not memory behaviour; the network must add information beyond it and beyond single-feature thresholds.

Control guest state: restore the database to a pre-seeded plateau at group start, record order counts and table size before and after each session (lab/guest_state.py already reports them), start each group on a fresh QEMU process and interleave roles over time. Re-enable realistic timers only as seeded, jittered jobs of a profile.
open_questions: Is the thesis claim about one server type or about generalisation across server types? This decides whether profiles are all in train and test or one is held out.
Is an endless restart loop (catalog typo for up to six minutes) a wanted benign event, or should restart loops be bounded by a start limit as on typical production units?
Should train and calibration contain event-free sessions and a no-op control? The current plan has events in all 96 sessions.
How many VM hours may the v5 campaign take (96 h per protocol now)? Four profiles mean fewer sessions per profile or a longer campaign.
May the guest PostgreSQL configuration be changed (autovacuum_naptime, logging), and may log rotation and similar maintenance return as seeded jobs of normal operation?
Should a replacement session keep its seed and events (composition preserved, deterministic failures repeat) or use a pre-registered derived seed?
Should the database start every group from a fixed snapshot (reproducible) or be allowed to age over the campaign (realistic but non-stationary)?
Is sshd available in the guest image for simulated admin logins, or must admin activity run through the guest agent? Unverified: the repository does not show it.
